name: Nucleus Software Exports Ltd
title: Nucleus Software Exports Ltd - 531209 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Nucleus Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 227.7 cr (+6.7% YoY) but EBITDA margin only 6.8% vs 10.8% a year ago; order book Rs 1,317 cr, yet no capacity or supply signal and DSO jumped to 80 days from 63.

triggers.label: DSO 63 → 80 days
triggers.quote: DSO stands at 80 days as compared to 63 days on June 30th, 2026.

triggers.label: Order book Rs 1,317 cr vs 1,244 cr
triggers.quote: Order book position as on September 30, 2026 is Rs. 1,317 crore, out of which 90% is product and 10% is projects.

triggers.label: Margin 6.8% vs 10.8% YoY
triggers.quote: Margins during the quarter is 6.8% as compared to 3.6% QoQ and 10.8% YoY.

red_flags.label: DSO up to 80 days from 63; receivables Rs 220.4 cr vs 174.7 cr
red_flags.quote: Receivables at Rs. 220.4 crore on 30th September, 2026 as against Rs. 174.7 crore on 30th June, 2026.

red_flags.label: Margin compression with rising employee cost
red_flags.quote: the margins for last so many quarters, the margins are not improving and the employee cost is going up.

red_flags.label: Order book methodology questioned, not clearly answered
red_flags.quote: Never. We have always maintained the same practice.

evasions.topic: Order book composition (AMC vs new licence)
evasions.quote: This order book, we don't give the backup of this AMC and other revenues.

evasions.quote: While I can't really give you the future guidelines on these numbers
once this gets stabilized, obviously margin will also see a reflection of that will be seen in the margins in the coming quarters.

summary.headline: Nucleus Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.7% YoY to Rs 227.7 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 10.8% a year ago.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 227.7 crore, up 8.2% QoQ and 6.7% YoY, though USD revenue fell 1.9% YoY to USD 24 million. EBITDA rose to Rs 15.4 crore from Rs 7.6 crore QoQ but remained well below Rs 23.1 crore a year earlier, and PAT fell 19.2% YoY to Rs 21.3 crore. Order book rose to Rs 1,317 crore from Rs 1,244 crore QoQ, with 90% product. Receivables and DSO rose sharply, with DSO at 80 days versus 63 days in Q1. Management gave no revenue guidance and repeatedly deferred questions on when revenue would break out of the Rs 200-220 crore quarterly range.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 7.6 crore QoQ (3.6%) and Rs 23.1 crore YoY (10.8%)
vs Rs 174.7 crore / 63 days on June 30, 2026

segments.name: Product revenue
segments.commentary: Product share of revenue was 84.4% in Q2 versus 83.9% in Q1; H1 product share was 84.2% versus 84.9% a year earlier.

segments.name: Geography (Q2)
segments.commentary: India 57.3% (Q1 56.1%), Middle East 12.4%, Southeast Asia 11%, Europe 5.7%. Management said the Europe growth reflects onboarding people for one customer and is a very small share of revenue.

segments.name: Top five clients
segments.commentary: Contributed 27% of Q2 revenue versus 28.1% in Q1; H1 share was 27.3% versus 26.8% a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or earnings guidance given; management said it cannot give future guidance on revenue numbers.
Management said the order book will reflect in revenue in subsequent quarters as projects run in parallel across India, SEA and the Middle East.
Management said margins should improve once AI investments and internal AI strategy stabilise, without giving a timeline.
Implementation cycles were described as 3 to 18 months, sometimes up to two years.
Pricing on the Rs 1,200-1,300 crore of orders won over the last three quarters was described as range-bound on a blended basis.
capex_capacity: Launched FinnOne Neo 9.0 and FinnAxia 9.0 in Vietnam with partner FPT at the first Nucleus Synapse customer event.
Transformation of the legacy product base onto FinnOne Neo is ongoing; management said the timeline is hard to predict and it remains a focus for the next financial year.
Five new logos added in the last six months (three in Q1, two in Q2).
Headcount 2,066 at September 30, 2026, versus 2,059 at June 30, 2026.
Forward covers of USD 2.5 million at an average rate of Rs 96.87 per USD as of September 30, 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book is up Rs 73 crore QoQ to Rs 1,317 crore; management does not split AMC/renewal from new licence and implementation value.
Management said the company has won roughly Rs 1,200-1,300 crore of orders over the last three quarters, with the geographic mix in line with current revenue.
Management said competition is not affecting pricing or win rates.
AMC is billed in advance, and a late-month AMC billing in Q2 pushed receivables up; management called this an aberration that should be collected within 10-15 days.
Management said the order book methodology has not changed, but it did not give a clear breakdown of AMC value included.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is new licence and implementation versus AMC renewals, and has the order book methodology changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not provide a split. It said some contracts carry five years of AMC in the book and others only one year, and that the methodology has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: When will revenue break out of the Rs 200-220 crore quarterly range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is one of the highest quarters in six, matching the revenue of seven quarters earlier at Rs 228 crore, and that the order book will reflect in future quarters. It gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the company run two platforms and two cost centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is one lending cost centre and that transformation timing is difficult to predict, but it remains a focus for the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost rising and will margins improve in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited AI talent hiring at higher market rates, the labour code change and new RSU policy. It said margins should improve once the AI strategy stabilises, but gave no H2 timeline. Annual increments had already been implemented and were not yet factored in.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables and deferred revenue growth rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said late-month AMC billing in Q2 raised receivables and was collected within 10-15 days. Advance AMC billing also raised the liability line.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Europe growth and can it be replicated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the growth is tied to one customer where people were onboarded, with no specific strategy, and Europe is a very small share of revenue.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin of 6.8% versus 10.8% a year ago, with cost of delivery and marketing spend both rising.
DSO of 80 days versus 63 in Q1, and receivables up Rs 45.7 crore QoQ; a late-month AMC billing is cited as the cause.
USD revenue down 1.9% YoY; H1 USD revenue down 6.9%.
Quarterly revenue has stayed in a Rs 200-220 crore range for about 12 quarters; the order book conversion timing remains unclear.
Cash fell by Rs 35.8 crore QoQ to Rs 942.1 crore, and other income is declining as mark-to-market gains on mutual funds shrink.
Top-five client concentration at 27% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about the order book, product recognition and AI strategy, but evasive on margins, revenue timing and the order book breakdown. It repeatedly said it cannot give forward numbers and that AI benefits will show up later without dates.
key_quotes: Healthy order book reflects our preference from the customer side for our product.

While I can't really give you the future guidelines on these numbers, I can only mention that we have a healthy order book, and we have a healthy implementation cycle, and that will start reflecting in future quarters.
We don't have AI as a revenue stream.

growth.why: No revenue or earnings guidance given; order book rose to Rs 1,317 crore (90% product) with management saying it will flow into revenue in later quarters, but no split of AMC versus new licence value and no timeline, so growth outlook is flat to unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: H2 FY27 at the earliest, no timeline given
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 10.8% a year ago and H1 margin is 5.3% vs 13.2%, with cost of delivery at 73.8% of revenue; management says margins improve once AI investments stabilise but gave no timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book rose to Rs 1,317 crore from Rs 1,244 crore QoQ (90% product) with management saying it will flow into later-quarter revenue, but H1 USD revenue fell 6.9% YoY and quarterly revenue has stayed in the Rs 200-220 crore range for about 12 quarters.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue or earnings guidance and declined to give forward revenue numbers, while H1 PAT fell 26.6% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: No guidance exists to cut, but margin pressure (EBITDA 6.8% vs 10.8% YoY), rising marketing spend (11% of revenue) and DSO at 80 days vs 63 leave downside risk to earnings expectations.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FinnOne Neo 9.0 and FinnAxia 9.0 were launched in Vietnam with partner FPT at the Nucleus Synapse customer event; legacy transformation onto FinnOne Neo is ongoing with no date, expected to remain a focus next fiscal year.

rows.label: Order book conversion into revenue
rows.why: Order book Rs 1,317 crore (up Rs 73 crore QoQ) is expected to reflect in later quarters, but no split of AMC vs new licence value was given and implementation cycles run 3 to 18 months, sometimes two years.

rows.label: DSO normalisation after late AMC billing
rows.why: DSO rose to 80 days from 63 and receivables rose Rs 45.7 crore QoQ to Rs 220.4 crore; management called it an aberration to be collected within 10-15 days.

rows.label: AI talent and employee cost pressure
rows.why: Cost of delivery rose 4.7% QoQ to 73.8% of revenue on AI hiring at higher market rates, labour code change and new RSU policy, and annual increments are not yet in the numbers.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, product recognition and AI strategy but evasive on margins, revenue timing and the AMC split of the order book, repeatedly declining forward numbers; analysts pressed on the Rs 200-220 crore revenue range and the order book breakdown.
